status: pre-execution. Supersedes qsigma_r6k_w1_partb_effective_protocol.json, which superseded qsigma_r6k_w1_partb_interval_correction.json. Where any of the three differ, this one governs.

supersession.added_by: R1R. The back-pointer only; no clause of this manifest was altered. The forward 'supersedes' declarations already existed and this side of the link did not, so a reader arriving here first had no signal.
supersession.unchanged: Part B has never been run. This stamp records document supersession and asserts nothing about execution.

reason: The previous effective protocol wrote its outcome table as English and the English contradicted itself in four ways, all found externally. A table decided by whoever reads it is an unfrozen threshold wearing a schema. The table is now a FUNCTION -- src/aionq/part_b_outcome.py -- total over its declared inputs, and this manifest quotes it rather than restating it. Restating it is how the two copies came to disagree.

execution_precondition.requirement: R6l C_env must be SEALED AND VERIFIED on origin. C_exec and C_raw reaching origin is not sufficient.
execution_precondition.why_the_previous_wording_was_wrong: the earlier manifests said part B becomes executable when C_exec and C_raw reach origin. Raw artifacts without their envelope are numbers with no commit binding, no digest binding and no declared verifier -- exactly the state this whole round was opened to repair in R6k. Part B may not consume upstream evidence weaker than the evidence it intends to produce.
execution_precondition.checkable: the R6l C_env commit must exist on origin, its envelope must verify, and its declared raw artifacts must resolve at its recorded commit with matching bytes

the_outcome_table_is_code.totality: every input either returns one of INVALID, REFUTED, INCONCLUSIVE, SUPPORTING with a stated reason, or raises. No input falls through to a default.
the_four_self_contradictions_it_removes: 0.296392 was said to lie inside the bracket (0.30, 0.40). It does not; 0.296392 < 0.30. Only (0.25, 0.30) contains it.
the prose made a first pass at 0.40 INCONCLUSIVE while the lookup table in the same document made 0.40 REFUTED.
a B3 failure -- the information margin going negative at a held-out depth -- had no outcome at all.
K9 -- clean and noisy slices disagreeing about the crossing -- had no typed outcome either.

frozen_margins.gate: INCLUSIVE, >= 0, on both. NOT strictly positive.
frozen_margins.why_this_matters: the previous manifest wrote the probability gate as strictly positive. A strict gate is a different gate: delta_P exactly 1/16 is representable in binary64 and the two rules disagree there. These are R6l's own gates, taken verbatim.
frozen_margins.arithmetic: IEEE-754 binary64 throughout, unrounded. 1/16 is exact; 0.02 is the nearest double and is used exactly as R6l uses it. Neither side is rounded before comparison.

bracket_rule.definition: the crossing is localised to (previous grid depth, first passing depth); when the first pass is 0.15 the lower edge is R6l's own 0.1, the nearest measured depth below it

trichotomy.inside: every point of the bracket is admissible -> SUPPORTING
trichotomy.straddling: an admissible-interval endpoint falls within the bracket, so the grid cannot say which side the crossing is on -> INCONCLUSIVE, and it may not be resolved by adding depths after seeing the data
trichotomy.outside: no point of the bracket is admissible, so the crossing is inadmissible wherever in it it falls -> REFUTED, not INCONCLUSIVE

expected_classification_by_first_passing.note: asserted as a parametrised test against the function, so the table and the code cannot drift apart the way the prose and the lookup did

measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.r6l_source_commit: PENDING -- the R6l C_exec commit SHA, recorded here before part B runs
measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.r6l_c_env_commit: PENDING -- the R6l C_env commit SHA, recorded here before part B runs
measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.r6l_result_digest: PENDING -- sha256 of the R6l result artifact at C_env
measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.r6l_envelope_digest: PENDING -- sha256 of the R6l envelope at C_env
measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.source_ring_inputs: PENDING -- the exact winding-ring source points R6l uses, by digest
measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.receiver_construction: the pooled map-blind PGM rebuilt at each held-out depth from R6l's recipe, uniform priors, ambient dimension 16. Reusing a receiver fitted at an original depth is forbidden; that measures transfer, not the crossing.
measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.noise_slice: the CLEAN slice only -- state-noise 0.0 and receiver-label-noise 0.0. The other fifteen coordinates are recorded and reported, never used to decide.
measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.aggregation: none. One margin per (depth, noise coordinate) cell, as R6l emits.
measurement_inputs_that_must_be_frozen_b.rule: part B MAY NOT EXECUTE while any field above reads PENDING. Filling them requires the R6l C_env artifacts, which is why the precondition is C_env and not C_raw.

preregistration_ordering_binding.note: the outcome FUNCTION src/aionq/part_b_outcome.py is co-committed with this manifest and is deliberately NOT claimed as preregistered by it -- the manifest quotes the function, so the function must exist for the manifest to be checkable at all. What this manifest preregisters is the part B EXECUTION, which has never run: files_expected_to_change names that surface, none of it exists, and aionq.self_audit.preregistration_ordering therefore reports status 'pending' rather than 'holds' or 'violated'.

typed_remainder.carrier: a table restated in two places
typed_remainder.comparison: the prose table and the lookup table disagreed about rho = 0.40 while sitting in one document. Two copies of a rule drift; one copy quoted from executable code cannot. That is why this manifest points at a function instead of describing one.

five measurement inputs are unfrozen because the artifacts that would fix them are not on origin. Part B is blocked on those, not merely waiting for them, and the block is mechanical: the fields read PENDING and the protocol forbids execution while they do.

typed_remainder.carrier: one ring, one slice, one grid
typed_remainder.comparison: a SUPPORTING outcome would be a numerical coincidence of two curves at a single winding ring, in a single noise slice, on a five-point grid with two brackets INCONCLUSIVE by construction. Held-out rings are the next thing it would need.
